function: no_learning (p. 4): the RIS phase shifts and power come from relaxation and alternating optimization (SDR, closed form); the LLM is only asserted for RB allocation and decoding order.
notes: The PDF is the paper of the DOI (p. 1: "Digital Object Identifier 10.1109/TVT.2024.3395748"), published version. The only learning is an LLM asserted in one paragraph, p. 4: "LLM can deduce optimized strategies for RB allocation and signal decoding order". No model, prompt, training, or inference procedure is given, and the paper then takes both as given (p. 4: "when {un,k} and {πn,k} is given"). The RIS phase shifts and power control are classical: p. 4: "a relaxation strategy is employed to find a sub-optimal solution"; p. 5: "applying the semidefinite relaxation (SDR) technique", with Gaussian randomization and closed-form power (eqs. 19-20). The simulations (pp. 5-8) never use the LLM. Figs. 3-6 sweep the RIS size and geometry, and Figs. 7-8 (pp. 7-8) compare "Initial phase shift optimization", "Random phase shift optimization", and "Without RIS". So learning appears only as framing. Even at face value, the stated LLM role (assigning vehicles to time RBs, and the SIC decoding order) would be scheduling (above_phy) or outside the seven areas (function), so the exclusion holds under either reading, and no_learning is the first code that applies. System: single-antenna BS and vehicles with a reflecting RIS, uplink NOMA (p. 3). p. 7 calls the vehicles' y coordinate a "flight altitude", but the system is an IoV of road vehicles (pp. 1-3). Either way, no_learning applies first.
